authorized_scope: CENSUS ONLY — no repair, consolidation, migration, deletion, rename, normalization or redesign
verification_rule: every mechanism is bound to a file, runtime artifact, persisted record or executable behaviour; anything unproven is marked UNKNOWN

IN_REPO.note: git-tracked — the ONLY JARVIS memory that travels between machines

DOCS.note: unindexed prose — the dominant JARVIS memory in practice

POSTGRES.note: ABSENT for JARVIS. agent_runs / integration_passes are MAIA Corpus Callosum tables, not JARVIS. No JARVIS mechanism in this census reads or writes PostgreSQL.

mechanisms.name: repo-markers
mechanisms.purpose: The single definition of what makes a directory a canonical Sovereign checkout (four markers).
mechanisms.provenance: extracted from main.js at JARVIS-00 (commit d5d3a15)
known_limits: marker presence is existence-only; it does not prove the checkout is functional

mechanisms.name: desktop-repo-resolution
mechanisms.purpose: Decide which repository the Desktop operates against; report which rung answered.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: in-memory per launch (RESOLVED), rebindable at runtime
mechanisms.authority: binds the READ plane; cannot grant execution authority
mechanisms.provenance: RESOLUTION vocabulary: explicit-env | explicit-config | implicit-default | dev-walk | unresolved
mechanisms.restart_survival: re-derived each launch; durable only via repo-config
known_limits: ends at a hard-coded DEFAULT candidate reported DEGRADED — deliberate for a viewer

mechanisms.name: jarvis-binding
mechanisms.purpose: The runtime's canonical repository binding: verified, provenance-carrying, refusing.
mechanisms.authority: binds the WRITE plane; refuses rather than defaulting (REPO_BINDING_UNRESOLVED)
mechanisms.provenance: reuses Desktop RESOLUTION vocabulary; reports divergence from the Desktop's saved binding as a fact
mechanisms.restart_survival: YES — binding.json read by a later process
known_limits: no DEFAULT rung by design
appData mapping mirrors Electron rather than sharing it — drift would surface as a differing config_path

mechanisms.name: repo-config
mechanisms.purpose: Persist the founder's explicit repository choice across launches and reboots.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: JSON file on local disk, atomic temp+rename
mechanisms.authority: FOUNDER CHOICE — the only explicit-founder persistence in JARVIS
mechanisms.provenance: version, repo_root, set_at, set_by; re-verified against markers on every read
known_limits: outside the repo — not versioned, not portable, not backed up
one binding per machine, no per-project bindings

mechanisms.name: first-run-prompt-ack
mechanisms.purpose: Record that the founder was asked to bind a repository, separately from whether they did.
mechanisms.provenance: prompted_at, outcome
known_limits: deliberately NOT merged into config: a declined prompt is not a binding

mechanisms.name: binding-record
mechanisms.purpose: What this runtime bound to, so a later process can answer what an earlier one believed.
mechanisms.provenance: root, resolution, explicit, markers_verified, config_path, divergence, substrate{head,branch,dirty}, pid, previous_root, rebound_since_last_run
current_consumers: JARVIS-00 proof; no production consumer yet
known_limits: keeps only the latest + previous root, not a full binding history
no consumer reads it at runtime yet — written for evidence, not yet for behaviour

mechanisms.name: work-packet
mechanisms.purpose: The canonical, attempt-invariant definition of one bounded piece of intended work.
mechanisms.writer: human/orchestrator authoring; runtime pipeline stamps runtime_run_id + worktree
mechanisms.authority: AUTHORITATIVE — carries governing_authority, authorized_acts, not_authorized_acts, autonomy_ceiling
mechanisms.provenance: canonical_sha binds the packet to a commit; established_facts[] carries prior knowledge
mechanisms.lifetime: durable; survives worker change, retry, escalation, transcript loss
known_limits: AUTHORED, never retrieved — established_facts[] is hand-written per packet; nothing assembles it from prior work
'proposed' vs 'ready' folded; deployment states unreachable

mechanisms.name: work-unit-derivation
mechanisms.purpose: Assemble packet + session + result(s) into one deterministic answer to 'what is this Work Unit right now', with no transcript.
mechanisms.authority: derives lifecycle; derivePermissionEnvelope() is provider-agnostic and never widens authority
mechanisms.provenance: each derived state names the files it was derived from
known_limits: documented folds: proposed/ready, claimed/running, verifying/review/ready-to-integrate
dependencies recorded but do not drive lifecycle
deployment + superseded states UNREACHABLE by derivation

mechanisms.name: result-record
mechanisms.purpose: The latest execution attempt's structured outcome.
mechanisms.provenance: escalation_required, test_results, exit_code, duration_s, ts
known_limits: single-file: the previous attempt is lost unless record-attempt was run first
worker self-report (escalation_required) is explicitly treated as worthless by the pipeline

mechanisms.name: attempts-history
mechanisms.purpose: Additive history of every recorded attempt at a Work Unit.
mechanisms.provenance: snapshot of result.json at record time
known_limits: APERTURE: population requires an explicit manual `record-attempt` call — nothing in the delegate or runtime path invokes it, so history is empty unless someone remembers

mechanisms.name: episodes-ledger
mechanisms.purpose: Append-only ledger of delegate runs.
readers: UNKNOWN — no reader located in scripts/builder or jarvis-desktop
mechanisms.provenance: ts, work_unit_id, lane, escalation_required, test_results, exit_code, duration_s
known_limits: named 'episodes' but is a run log, NOT a Work Episode in the directive’s sense: no objective, no starting state, no actions, no evidence refs
no located consumer — write-only as far as this census can prove

mechanisms.name: delegate-logs
mechanisms.purpose: Raw worker transport logs per delegate run.
mechanisms.provenance: unstructured
known_limits: unstructured; not machine-adjudicated

mechanisms.name: runtime-run-records
mechanisms.purpose: One file per runtime-driven run: state machine position, packet ref, worktree, evidence refs.
mechanisms.authority: evidentiary; run state is not authority
mechanisms.provenance: REFERENCES packet/result/log paths rather than copying them — one audit artifact per run
mechanisms.restart_survival: YES — explicitly designed for it ('restarting must not destroy durable run history')
known_limits: listRuns loads every run file to sort — unbounded read cost as history grows
no index, no query beyond newest-first

mechanisms.name: runtime-events
mechanisms.purpose: Append-only transition log for run state changes.
mechanisms.provenance: timestamped transitions
known_limits: writes are best-effort and silently dropped on failure — cannot be relied on as evidence
no located reader

mechanisms.name: runtime-process-record
mechanisms.purpose: Current/last runtime process record.
mechanisms.provenance: process record
known_limits: a killed runtime cannot rewrite its own record — hence orphan reconciliation

mechanisms.name: orphan-reconciliation
mechanisms.purpose: At next start, mark runs left mid-flight by a hard stop as FAILED/RUNTIME_STOPPED_MID_RUN.
mechanisms.provenance: sets reconciled_at + failure_class
known_limits: 'an in-flight state is not evidence of a running worker once the owning process is gone' — correct, but the underlying worker is not actually killed

mechanisms.name: builder-session-records
mechanisms.purpose: One governed Builder session: ownership of a branch/worktree, model recorded, heartbeat, collision state.
mechanisms.authority: CLAIM AUTHORITY — governs ownership; refuses, never kills
mechanisms.provenance: unit, branch, worktree, model, read-only flag, state, timestamps
known_limits: only sessions that explicitly `open` are governed — an ungoverned `claude` process is invisible by design
does not know subscription quota units

mechanisms.name: builder-session-ledger
mechanisms.purpose: Append-only ledger of Builder session lifecycle events.
mechanisms.provenance: event stream
known_limits: session-scoped only; carries no work content

mechanisms.name: concurrency-state
mechanisms.purpose: Current concurrency governance state (lanes active, bands).
mechanisms.authority: CAPABILITY/CAPACITY state — distinct from claim state
mechanisms.provenance: derived from session records
known_limits: measures sessions/hours/rate, not provider quota units

mechanisms.name: worktree-claim
mechanisms.purpose: One active write lane -> one branch -> one worktree -> one owner.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: git worktree on disk + PID lockfile
mechanisms.provenance: branch + base_sha at claim
known_limits: PID-file fallback rather than flock (no flock on the Mac Studio dev host) — a stale PID needs explicit recovery
worktrees are development substrates and are expected to disappear

mechanisms.name: rate-observability
mechanisms.purpose: Measure request RATE (the variable that actually failed on 2026-08-09), not concurrency weight.
mechanisms.provenance: measured from ledger timestamps
known_limits: local proxy; provider-side quota not observable

mechanisms.name: context-materialization
mechanisms.purpose: Select LESS THAN A WHOLE FILE, materialize the bytes with provenance, refuse when the packet would not fit.
mechanisms.writer: materializePacket() (in-memory fragments handed to the worker)
mechanisms.persistence_medium: EPHEMERAL — fragments are not persisted; re-derived on demand
mechanisms.provenance: file, start, end, selector, source_sha (SHA-bound), sha256 of content
mechanisms.cross_session_survival: NO (but deterministically reproducible from packet + sha)
known_limits: selectors are lines/symbol/file — no semantic or dependency-aware selection
budget is a token estimate, not a measurement

mechanisms.name: evidence-verification
mechanisms.purpose: Mechanically re-derive the fragments the worker was shown and check every citation against them.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: verdict stored on the run record
mechanisms.provenance: each citation -> in_context bool + fragment + source_sha
known_limits: proves a citation was IN the shown context — not that the conclusion drawn from it is correct
never consults the worker's self-assessment (deliberate: 'the self-report is worthless')

mechanisms.name: packet-guard
mechanisms.purpose: Refuse answer-leaking packets and bind every selector to a SHA before a worker is invoked.
mechanisms.provenance: bindSelector + headOf
current_consumers: runtime pipeline (lints FIRST, before any worktree claim)
known_limits: lexical leakage detection — a semantically leaking packet that avoids the patterns would pass

mechanisms.name: deterministic-registry
mechanisms.purpose: C0 lane: answer a task with a deterministic capability, zero LLM.
mechanisms.provenance: each capability declares its own args schema
known_limits: small fixed registry; no code-graph or repo-structure capability

mechanisms.name: run-check
mechanisms.purpose: Structured deterministic verification wrapper: status from exit_code, never from stdout text.
mechanisms.writer: emits JSON result attachable to a Work Unit
mechanisms.persistence_medium: JSON on stdout; attached by caller
mechanisms.provenance: exit_code, status, sha, duration_ms, work_unit
known_limits: no automatic attachment — the caller must persist it

mechanisms.name: epistemic-claim-records
mechanisms.purpose: A durable, versioned claim: assertion + status + cited evidence.
mechanisms.authority: claims carry epistemic STANDING, not execution authority
mechanisms.provenance: evidence[] entries with kind + detail + ref
known_limits: ONE claim exists today (.ain/claims/001-guard-proof-at-admission.json) — the mechanism is proven, the corpus is empty
authored by hand; nothing derives a claim from a completed run

mechanisms.name: epistemic-ledger
mechanisms.purpose: Append-only record of status transitions and corrections.
mechanisms.authority: the canonical prior-history source for CI adjudication
mechanisms.provenance: type, ts, prior_authoritative_rows, begins_at, enforcement_mode, reason, scope
known_limits: 2 rows today — mechanism proven, corpus effectively empty

mechanisms.name: epistemic-guard
mechanisms.purpose: Adjudicate ONE claim: refuse promotion when cited evidence cannot carry the requested status.
mechanisms.authority: REFUSES promotion (exit 1 is a verdict, not an error). Not a fact checker, not a ratifier.
mechanisms.provenance: 8 statuses (OBSERVATION/PROVEN/CORRECTION/HEURISTIC/INVARIANT/HYPOTHESIS/STALE/SUPERSEDED); RANK{HYPOTHESIS0,OBSERVATION1,PROVEN2,INVARIANT3}; 22 evidence kinds split WEAK/PROBATIVE; standing PROBATIVE|WEAK|NON_PROBATIVE|STALE; 7 guards G1-G7; 7 correction rungs
known_limits: adjudicates one claim at a time — no cross-claim dependency or cascade
`scan` is advisory prose triage, deliberately weaker
correction->doctrine promotion is candidate-only by directive

mechanisms.name: epistemic-ci
mechanisms.purpose: Authoritative admission gate: PR supplies the claim, canonical supplies prior history, CI recomputes adjudication.
mechanisms.provenance: invokes epistemic-guard as a subprocess so the admitted guard blob stays byte-identical
known_limits: gates claims that are OFFERED; nothing requires a claim to be offered for a given change

mechanisms.name: desktop-provenance
mechanisms.purpose: Two independent identity facts, never collapsed: ARTIFACT ('I am build X') and SUBSTRATE ('I operate against root@head, dirty').
mechanisms.authority: reporting discipline; DEGRADED for an unnamed binding
mechanisms.provenance: RESOLUTION vocabulary is defined here and reused by the runtime binding
known_limits: build stamp is null in dev by design (guard: unpackaged returns null before touching disk)

mechanisms.name: governance-gate
mechanisms.purpose: Let a worker say in structured form: 'I cannot truthfully continue because this requires authority I do not possess.'
mechanisms.authority: PAUSES, does not fail — non-terminal by design; the objective stays open
mechanisms.provenance: structured gate emission, not harness-manufactured
known_limits: Unit 18 earned Classification C on this seam — the 'ask' used to be manufactured by the harness

mechanisms.name: legibility-derivation
mechanisms.purpose: Pure derivation of the founder-facing view from the status object the mechanism already produces.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: NONE — computes nothing about the world
mechanisms.authority: none — promotes facts, never invents them
mechanisms.provenance: every fact promoted from jarvis:status
known_limits: cannot show what jarvis:status does not carry — renders UNKNOWN instead

mechanisms.name: living-spiral-projection
mechanisms.purpose: Render the governed derivation as a spiral. PROJECTION ONLY.
mechanisms.persistence_medium: NONE — 'not a verifier, not an authority source, not a telemetry source, and not a state store'
mechanisms.provenance: single input: legibility.deriveOperatorView(); renders an APERTURE when it cannot know
known_limits: implements the operational_element vocabulary only — the semantic contract's §9 epistemic grammar is NOT implemented here
motion renders UNOBSERVED: JOP-05A (lawful temporal source) is unbound

mechanisms.name: living-spiral-semantic-contract
mechanisms.purpose: Ratified semantics for operational element/layer, motion, stillness, disturbance, absence, temporal, EPISTEMIC and PROVENANCE grammar.
mechanisms.scope: JARVIS operator domain ONLY (R1); a member is never an inferred node (R2)
mechanisms.authority: RATIFIED semantics; implementation authority granted by later founder ruling 2026-08-16
mechanisms.provenance: §10 requires every assertion to carry source, resolver, binding_method
known_limits: §9 epistemic grammar (established/provisional/emerging/ambiguous/contradicted/superseded/unknown + 5 evidence_classes) has NO executable implementation
header still stamps 'IMPLEMENTATION NOT AUTHORIZED', preserved as history and superseded by later ruling — two coexisting facts

mechanisms.name: router
mechanisms.purpose: C0 (deterministic) / C1 (bounded local) / C3 (escalate). Deliberately NOT an intent classifier.
mechanisms.provenance: a task states its own capability (checked against the real registry) or declares bounded_for_local
known_limits: no C2 lane exists at this stage
routes on declared properties, never on prior experience — nothing consults history to decide a lane

mechanisms.name: ops-proof-records
mechanisms.purpose: Durable narrative record of proofs, corrections, reconciliations and rulings.
mechanisms.authority: records founder rulings; some are ratified canon
mechanisms.provenance: each names its own evidence and date
known_limits: THE dominant JARVIS memory today, and it is unindexed prose: retrievable only by filename guess or grep
no machine link between a doc and the claim/run it attests

mechanisms.name: claude-agents
mechanisms.purpose: Named agent role definitions (ain-architect, maia-dev, maia-ops, maia-ios, ain-growth, security-auditor).
mechanisms.authority: scopes an agent's tools; does not grant JARVIS authority
mechanisms.provenance: frontmatter
known_limits: harness-level, NOT JARVIS: no JARVIS runtime reads these
no procedure, no STOP conditions, no validation, no version history — a role, not a Skill primitive

mechanisms.name: claude-commands
mechanisms.purpose: Reusable prompt templates invoked as slash commands (oracle-*, db, migration-upgrade, testing-pattern…).
mechanisms.provenance: none recorded
known_limits: THE CLOSEST EXISTING THING TO A SKILL PRIMITIVE, and it is a prompt: no trigger conditions, prerequisites, authority requirements, hazards, STOP conditions, validation procedure, expected evidence, examples, version, or provenance
not derived from verified work — hand-authored

mechanisms.name: claude-plans
mechanisms.purpose: Build plans authored during planning sessions.
mechanisms.provenance: none recorded
known_limits: random-slug filenames carry no subject — unaddressable without opening each
no link to any Work Unit, run, or claim

mechanisms.name: claude-project-memory
mechanisms.purpose: Named project memories referenced by key from CLAUDE.md (e.g. project_sacred_learning).
mechanisms.persistence_medium: markdown files under a machine-path-derived directory
mechanisms.provenance: none recorded in the files
known_limits: CLAUDE.md cites memory keys NOT present here (project_anchor_consent_gate_live, project_corpus_callosum_substrate_cat6, project_six_category_artifact_typology) — the full store is elsewhere and UNPROVEN by this census
directory name hard-codes a machine path, so it does not travel
harness-level, NOT JARVIS: no JARVIS runtime reads it

mechanisms.name: session-anchor
mechanisms.purpose: The re-entry document: what the project is, invariants, current priority thread, ops diagnostics, known traps.
mechanisms.authority: states project invariants and vows; overrides default agent behaviour
mechanisms.provenance: dated entries; explicit six-category artifact typology
known_limits: MAIA-dominant: JARVIS appears only via 'Known recurring traps' and the builder scripts, not in the priority thread
hand-maintained; grows monotonically; no mechanism marks an entry stale
